title: Shortest Subarray With Bitwise OR at Least K
description: Given an array `nums` of non-negative integers and a non-negative integer `k`, a non-empty contiguous subarray is called special if the bitwise OR of all its elements is at least `k`. Return the length of the shortest special subarray of `nums`, or `-1` if no special subarray exists.
hints: Bitwise OR is monotonically non-decreasing as a window expands, so a two-pointer sliding window applies once you can remove elements from the left.
Maintain a 30-element array `bitCount[b]` tracking how many elements in the current window have bit `b` set; a bit drops from the window OR only when its count falls to `0`.

examples.explanation: The single-element subarray [2] (or [3]) already has bitwise OR >= 2, so the shortest length is 1.
Only the full subarray [2, 1, 8] achieves bitwise OR 11 >= 10, giving length 3.
Even the entire array [1, 2] has bitwise OR 3 < 4, so return -1.
